text:
Claire: Heads-up — we started seeing a cold-start hit-rate dip on prefix caching after yesterday's attn-layout-v2 + quant-profile B roll. Spike in first-50-token miss rate on a few high-QPS models :eyes:
Raj: rough numbers?
Claire: sample service 'text-gen-prod' — baseline warm-hit ~82% across requests, dropped to ~58% after the rollout for requests with long prompt prefixes. Latency not super worse but cost up.
perf-bot: Profiling snapshot uploaded — see inline.
perf-bot: ```prefix_cache.hits=580/1000
prefix_cache.warm_hits=120/1000
early_tokens.miss_rate.first20=0.62
kernel_variant=attn-layout-v2
quant_profile=per-tensor-8bit-bf16-fallback```
Sofie: repro steps: curl against canary cluster, repeated 200 RPS with mix of seeded prefixes. I saw identical behavior locally when enabling the new matmul layout.
Tomas: could be keying change — did we change tokenizer normalization or buildid inclusion?
Alex: we didn't change tokenizer. But attn-layout-v2 swaps padding order and reorders leading dims in the kernel. That can change the sequence-of-ops that feed into the key fingerprinting if we accidentally included runtime ordering in the key derivation (we shouldn't).
Claire: confirmed: our prefix key currently does sha1(prefix_bytes + model_build_id + seq_dim) — seq_dim is derived from runtime layout helper. That was never intended to be part of the key. It became noisy after the kernel layout swap.
Raj: Oof. So keys diverge across kernel variants even for identical logical prefixes. Explains warmup miss wave.
Sofie: quick mitigation: we can normalize seq_dim before hashing or drop it entirely. Is there any legit reason to vary keys per kernel layout?
Tomas: historically seq_dim was included to avoid cross-architecture collisions when shape packing changed. But we should use logical shape (token_count) not kernel internal layout tag.
Alex: I pushed a small patch on branch hotfix/prefix-key-normalize that replaces seq_dim with logical_length and strips layout_tag.
perf-bot: Perf regression delta after patch (canary): early_token_miss_rate.first20 -> 0.21 (from 0.62), warm_hits -> 800/1000, latency P95 unchanged.
Claire: Nice — can we do a quick AB: traffic pinned to patched canary vs current?
deploy-bot: Rolling canary: deploy hotfix/prefix-key-normalize to 10% -> 6078901250
Raj: Also want to audit other key inputs: build_id rolling semantics, tokenizer flags (strip/normalize), quant_profile id. Quant id should be part of key if it changes runtime output.
Tomas: Agreed. Quant profile affects output distribution, so it's valid to include. But kernel layout shouldn't.
Sofie: Noted an edge case — when we fallback from per-tensor-8bit to fp16 kernel, we should keep same logical quant id mapping or canonicalize it. Some customers flip profiles and we don't want accidental churn.
Alex: I'll add unit tests to ensure prefix-key is deterministic across kernel variants for same logical model+tokenizer+quant.
Claire: Next steps: 1) monitor canary for 1 hour, 2) audit key derivation doc + tests, 3) add migration script to repopulate cache for 24h hot prefixes if rollback not desired.
Raj: Also add a perf test that simulates mixed kernel fleet to ensure keys don't diverge under hybrid setups.
perf-bot: Note: we should capture KV cache hit telemetry tagged by kernel_variant and quant_profile to catch these earlier. Filed: INF-3247.
Claire: cool. If canary looks stable I'll promote to 50% and schedule full rollout window with SRE tomorrow. :thumbsup:
